en: Mayon Volcano in Albay has a permanent danger zone where people must not enter because sudden explosive eruptions can release deadly pyroclastic flows.
After heavy typhoon floods in Manila, children should avoid wading in contaminated street water to prevent leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection from rat urine.
If you feel a strong earthquake near the coasts of Batanes, immediately move to higher ground because a destructive tsunami wave might follow.
Hikers climbing Mt. Pulag in Benguet must bring thick jackets because the summit's temperature can drop below freezing, causing dangerous hypothermia.
During the rainy season, the Cagayan River can experience sudden flash floods, so locals must avoid crossing its fast-rising, muddy waters.
When swimming in the coral reefs of Tubbataha, wear water shoes to protect your feet from sharp rocks and venomous sea urchin spines.
Stagnant water left in old tires after the humid wet season breeds Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit the dangerous dengue virus to humans.
When Taal Volcano erupts, residents in Batangas must wear N95 masks because inhaling fine volcanic ash can cause severe respiratory breathing problems.
During the dry summer months in Metro Manila, the high heat index can cause heatstroke, so students must drink plenty of water.
The Valley Fault System cuts through Metro Manila, meaning houses built directly above this active geological fracture are at high risk of collapsing during earthquakes.
Trekking through the muddy trails of the Sierra Madre mountain range requires wearing long pants to prevent tropical land leeches from attaching to bare skin.
Boaters on Laguna de Bay should wear life jackets and check weather forecasts because sudden strong winds can quickly create dangerous, capsizing waves.
